tldr: In the self-inclusive equation-(2.2) panel subclass, the peer coefficient is identified from a realized conditional-mean schedule exactly when the observable anchored contrasts have a nonzero signed sum on some member-labelled component--group cycle, equivalently when \(Bx\ne0\). A nonzero cycle gives an explicit ratio; when every cycle sum vanishes, observable vertex potentials generate a continuum of equivalent coefficients. With fixed finite \(N,M,T\) and unrestricted schedule-conditional nuisance means, one informative support schedule is necessary and sufficient, and generic identification requires at least one support schedule with \(B\ne0\). The labelled-cycle certificate, linear block algorithm, and sharp zero-, one-, or two-edit unrestricted redesign frontier remain unchanged.
gap: The closest source gives a general null-space test and a sufficient generic rank cutoff, but the inspected literature does not characterize which member-labelled schedules pass or the smallest unrestricted membership change that repairs failure.
fill: Establish the pointwise and generic cycle criteria, a cycle-indexed observable functional, all-failure alternatives, the exact rank relation, an edge-ID-aware block certificate, and the sharp unrestricted edit frontier.
